title: Maasai Mara
subtitle: The Crown Jewel of African Safari
description: Home to the Great Migration and the Big Five, the Maasai Mara is Kenya's most celebrated wildlife reserve. Rolling golden savannas stretch to the horizon, dotted with acacia trees and teeming with an extraordinary density of wildlife.
shortDescription: Kenya's most iconic wildlife reserve, home to the Great Migration.

title: Diani Beach
subtitle: Paradise on the Indian Ocean
description: Consistently voted Africa's leading beach destination, Diani Beach stretches for 17 kilometers of pristine white sand backed by lush coastal forest. Crystal-clear turquoise waters offer world-class snorkeling, diving, and water sports.
shortDescription: Africa's leading beach destination with 17km of pristine white sand.

title: Nairobi
subtitle: The Green City in the Sun
description: Kenya's dynamic capital is the only city in the world with a national park within its borders. A cosmopolitan hub of culture, cuisine, and innovation, Nairobi offers everything from world-class dining to wildlife encounters just minutes from the city center.
shortDescription: Kenya's vibrant capital. The only city with a national park within its borders.

title: Amboseli
subtitle: Land of Giants
description: Famous for its large elephant herds and iconic views of Mount Kilimanjaro, Amboseli National Park offers some of Kenya's most photographed landscapes. Watch elephants walk in silhouette against Africa's highest peak.
shortDescription: Iconic elephant herds framed by the majestic Mount Kilimanjaro.

title: Lake Naivasha
subtitle: Jewel of the Rift Valley
description: A freshwater lake in the Great Rift Valley surrounded by papyrus and acacia forests. Lake Naivasha is a haven for birdwatchers with over 400 species, and Crescent Island offers one of Kenya's best walking safari experiences.
shortDescription: A serene freshwater lake in the Rift Valley, perfect for boat safaris and birdwatching.

title: Watamu
subtitle: Marine Paradise
description: A small coastal town with one of Kenya's finest marine parks. Watamu's protected coral reefs teem with tropical fish, sea turtles, and dolphins. The nearby Gede Ruins add a layer of historical mystery to this seaside gem.
shortDescription: Pristine marine park, coral reefs, and one of Kenya's best-kept coastal secrets.

title: Lamu
subtitle: UNESCO Heritage Island
description: One of the oldest inhabited towns in East Africa, Lamu Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Narrow winding streets, ancient Swahili architecture, and a pace of life unchanged for centuries make Lamu a truly unique destination.
shortDescription: A UNESCO World Heritage island with centuries-old Swahili culture and donkey-only streets.

title: Nanyuki
subtitle: Gateway to Mount Kenya
description: A charming highland town at the foot of Mount Kenya. Nanyuki serves as the base for Mount Kenya treks and is surrounded by some of Kenya's finest luxury ranches and conservancies, offering exclusive wildlife experiences.
shortDescription: Highland town at the foot of Mount Kenya, surrounded by luxury ranches and conservancies.

title: Lake Nakuru
subtitle: Flamingos, Rhinos & Rift Valley Views
description: Set within the floor of the Great Rift Valley, Lake Nakuru National Park is one of Kenya's most visually striking reserves. The alkaline lake draws vast flocks of flamingos that paint the shoreline pink, while the surrounding acacia woodland shelters both black and white rhinos, making it one of the best places in East Africa to see these endangered animals up close.
shortDescription: A Rift Valley gem known for its flamingo-lined shores and thriving rhino sanctuary.

title: Samburu
subtitle: Where the Wild North Begins
description: Samburu National Reserve sits in Kenya's arid north, bisected by the palm-fringed Ewaso Ng'iro River. This rugged landscape is home to the Samburu Special Five: Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, Beisa oryx, Somali ostrich, and the long-necked gerenuk. Far fewer visitors make it this far north, giving the reserve an intimate, off-the-beaten-path quality that is hard to find elsewhere in Kenya.
shortDescription: A remote northern reserve home to rare wildlife and the Samburu Special Five.

title: Tsavo
subtitle: Kenya's Untamed Wilderness
description: Together, Tsavo East and Tsavo West form the largest protected area in Kenya, covering over 20,000 square kilometres of diverse terrain. Tsavo West is known for its volcanic landscapes, lava flows, and the crystal-clear Mzima Springs, while Tsavo East offers vast open plains and the iconic Yatta Plateau. The park's elephants famously dust themselves in the region's red laterite soil, giving them their distinctive rust-coloured appearance.
shortDescription: Kenya's largest national park, famous for red elephants, lava flows, and untouched wilderness.

title: Laikipia
subtitle: Conservation at Its Finest
description: The Laikipia Plateau is Kenya's conservation success story. A patchwork of private ranches, community conservancies, and wildlife corridors, it supports the country's largest population of endangered black rhinos and the second-largest population of elephants. With far fewer tourists than the Mara, Laikipia offers exclusive walking safaris, night drives, and horseback rides through landscapes shared by Maasai, Samburu, and Laikipia communities.
shortDescription: A private conservancy region with exceptional rhino populations and exclusive safari experiences.

title: Hells Gate
subtitle: Walk Among the Wildlife
description: One of the few national parks in Kenya where you can explore entirely on foot or by bicycle, Hells Gate offers a completely different kind of safari. Towering red cliffs rise on either side as you cycle past zebras, giraffes, and buffalo grazing in the open valley. The park's Fischer's Tower and the narrow gorge with its geothermal hot springs add a geological drama that sets it apart from any other destination in the country.
shortDescription: A unique park where you walk and cycle among zebras, giraffes, and volcanic gorges.

title: Mombasa North Coast
subtitle: Where History Meets the Ocean
description: The North Coast stretches from Mombasa Island through Nyali, Bamburi, and Shanzu, offering a mix of resort luxury, historical depth, and local culture. Fort Jesus, a 16th-century Portuguese fortress and UNESCO World Heritage Site, anchors the old town, while the long sandy beaches of Nyali and Bamburi provide easy access to water sports, marine parks, and Haller Park's rescued wildlife. The North Coast is livelier and more connected to Mombasa's urban energy than its quieter southern counterpart.
shortDescription: Resort beaches, Fort Jesus, and the vibrant culture of Mombasa's northern coastline.
